caption: Huertas v. Bayer US LLC
citation_line: Huertas v. Bayer US LLC, No. 2:21-cv-20021, ECF No. 48 (D.N.J. May 23, 2023), rev’d in part, No. 23-2178 (3d Cir. Nov. 7, 2024)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Wigenton dismissed consumer claims arising from recalled Lotrimin and Tinactin sprays contaminated with benzene, applying a heightened conception of the economic injury required for Article III standing.
qualification_rationale: The case addresses standing for consumers who bought allegedly contaminated products but suffered no physical injury, an important and recurring question in pharmaceutical, food, product-recall, and putative class litigation.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit partially reversed in a precedential opinion, holding that the district court had imposed too demanding a standing standard on purchasers alleging an economic overpayment injury.
decision_selection_note: Appeal 23-2178, filed 2023. ECF 27 is the first dismissal.
